parole.significato: A Native American hostage taken by Russian colonists.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian амана́т (amanát, “hostage”), via a Turkic language from Arabic أَمَانَة (ʔamāna, “surety”).

parole.significato: A village encampment in the Caucasus, Central Asia or the Southern Urals.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian ау́л (aúl), from West (Kypchak) Turkic awul, awïl; compare Karachay-Balkar ауул (awul), Bashkir ауыл (awıl), Kazakh ауыл (awıl) and Turkish ağıl.

parole.significato: An arc-shaped shifting sand dune comprising well-sorted (uniformly sized) sand.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Russian барха́н (barxán), from a Turkic language such as Kazakh барқан (barqan); further etymology unknown. The Russian word was first used in scientific literature in 1881 by the Russian zoologist and explorer Alexander von Middendorf (1815–1894).

parole.significato: A type of Russian heavy draft horse, originally from Voronezh guberniya on the Bityug river.
parole.testo: From the name of the Bityug river near Voronezh, ultimately from Russian битю́г (bitjúg), which is from Turkic.

parole.significato: A medieval heroic warrior in Kievan Rus, akin to the Western European knight-errant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian богаты́рь (bogatýrʹ), Old East Slavic богатꙑрь (bogatyrĭ), from a Turkic language, probably Khazar, from Old Turkic [script needed] (baɣatur, “hero”), from Proto-Turkic *bagatur (“hero”). Cognates include Turkish bahadır, Tatar баһадир (bahadir), Chuvash паттӑр (pattăr), Kyrgyz
From Russian черке́с (čerkés), of disputed origin, with suggestions including Turkic or Mongolic. See Circassians.

parole.significato: a cauldron or cooking pot used in Central Asian cuisine
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian каза́н (kazán), from a Turkic language. Cognate with Azerbaijani qazan, Kazakh қазан (qazan), Turkish kazan, Uzbek qozon.

parole.significato: A subspecies of onager (Equus hemionus), Equus hemionus kulan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian кулан (kulan, “Asiatic wild ass”), ultimately from Turkic. Compare Ottoman Turkish قولان (kulan, “wild ass”), Kyrgyz кулан (kulan), Kazakh құлан (qulan), Karakalpak qulan, Nogai кулан (kulan), Bashkir ҡолан (qolan), Tatar колан (qolan), Uyghur قۇلان (qulan), Chagatai قولان (qwl

parole.significato: A prehistoric burial mound once used by peoples in Siberia and Central Asia.
parole.testo: From Russian курга́н (kurgán), from a Turkic language.

parole.significato: A traditional long, trapeze-shaped Russian pinafore worn by women and girls.
parole.testo: From Russian сарафа́н (sarafán), from Turkic, from Persian سراپا (sarâpâ, literally “from head to foot”). Doublet of sarapa.
From Russian сарлык (sarlyk), most likely from a Turkic source, see Tuvan сарлык (sarlık).

parole.significato: Either of two species of the amaranth genus Haloxylon: Haloxylon ammodendron (syn. Haloxylon aphyllum; black saxaul) an…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian саксау́л (saksaúl), via a Turkic variety (compare Bashkir саҡсауыл (saqsawıl), Kazakh сексеуіл (seksewil)), ultimately from Kalmyk [script needed] (zaɣzāml̥, “a bush growing in the desert”), compare Mongolian заг (zag, “saxaul”), Kalmyk за (za).

parole.significato: A fish (Cyprinus carpio) in the Cyprinidae family. It is native to Sea of Azov, Black Sea, Caspian Sea, Aral Sea, Balkh…
parole.testo: From Russian саза́н (sazán), from Turkic, from Proto-Turkic *siāŕgan (“carp; snake, dragon”).

parole.significato: A type of relief, a dry fissured crust primarily formed by filamentous cyanobacteria, occurring in the deserts of Centr…
parole.testo: From Russian такыр (takyr), from a Turkic source; compare Bashkir таҡыр (taqır).

parole.significato: An extinct Northern European wild horse, Equus ferus ferus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian тарпа́н (tarpán), from Turkic (Kazakh тарпаң (tarpaŋ) or Kyrgyz тарпан (tarpan)).

parole.significato: An in-kind tribute in Imperial Russia exacted from the indigenous peoples of Siberia, usually in fur.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian ясак (jasak), from Turkic, from Middle Mongol ᠵᠠᠰᠠᠭ (ǰasaɣ)

parole.significato: The natural resources and arable land over which a Cossack stanitsa had exclusive control in their territory.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian юрт (jurt), from a Turkic language in the sense of “one's native land”, from Proto-Turkic *yūrt (“dwelling place”).
